events.title: CISA Adds 3 Exploited Flaws to KEV: Drupal Core, Optimizely
events.summary: CISA added three actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog on 24 November 2026: a deserialization flaw in Idunno AntiCsrf, a remote code execution flaw in Drupal Core, and a critical state data manipulation flaw in Optimizely Web Experimentation.
events.why_it_matters: All three flaws show evidence of active exploitation, meaning patching is urgent rather than precautionary. Two carry published CVSS scores of 9.3 and 7.1, and the Drupal issue allows remote code execution. Under CISA's Binding Operational Directive, US federal agencies must prioritize security updates for KEV entries, and the catalog is widely used as a patching guide elsewhere.

reasons: published by an Australian government authority (ACSC Alerts)

events.title: PHP warns admins of two critical flaws, emergency patches coming tomorrow
events.summary: The PHP project has told administrators to ready themselves for emergency updates the following day fixing two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, after details of the flaws reportedly leaked early. Headline reporting also references exploit attempts and the fact that these follow other emergency PHP patches issued days earlier.
events.why_it_matters: One of the listed flaws carries a CNA-assigned CVSS score of 9.9, and headline reporting indicates exploit attempts have emerged. Because PHP powers a large share of web applications, defenders running PHP should plan to apply the emergency patches as soon as they are released.
